title: Active sessions with database, server, and role
description: For active sessions return exactly four columns: session_id, database_name, hostname, role_name. Join sessions to databases, servers, and db_roles by their identifiers. Sort by database_name ASC, then session_id ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT s.id AS session_id
FROM sessions AS s
hints: sessions has two links: to a database and a role; the database links to the server.
Apply the state filter to the session rows.
solution_explanation: Three joins reconstruct the active session context from normalized tables.
